assignmentModel.contract: The shipped scheduler accepts flat_pool and rejects wave activation before dispatch.

concurrency.contract: The configured cap is a positive integer no greater than eight and the async pool holds at most that many live lineages.

count.contract: A lineage count expands deterministically into one runnable unit per replica with collision-checked labels.

iterations.contract: Each lineage carries its own positive iteration cap; the default upper-bound calculation uses twelve when absent.

timeout.contract: Single dispatches use a bounded spawn timeout with SIGKILL; fan-out computes a bounded lineage timeout and reports signal termination as failure.

stdin.contract: Codex receives the prompt through stdin and the parent closes the pipe; headless background examples redirect from /dev/null.

budgets.contract: Aggregate cost is rejected before any lineage spawn and per-lineage cost is rejected inside the worker before provider execution.

cleanup.contract: Cleanup targets only captured process identifiers and descendants; blanket command-name kills are prohibited.

artifacts.contract: Each lineage writes into its own artifact directory; missing required reports or iteration files prevents fulfillment.

completionMarkers.contract: The prompt requests FANOUT_LINEAGE_COMPLETE:<label>, while durable report and iteration artifacts remain the stronger completion evidence.

recursionGuard.contract: SPECKIT_CLI_DISPATCH_STACK is stamped per dispatch and a same-kind child lineage is rejected before spawn.

incidentVerdicts.adapterDefect: A hermetic invocation reaches the shipped adapter contract and violates an asserted command, process, artifact, or classification invariant.
incidentVerdicts.dependencySkip: A gated live-only cell names the unavailable binary, authentication state, recursion signal, dependency realpath, or opt-in switch.
incidentVerdicts.harnessFailure: The fixture itself cannot establish its timeout, process ownership, isolated workspace, capture, or cleanup precondition.
